notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, as the county reported them in its Annual Financial Report to the Iowa Department of Management. Not a budget.

Debt outstanding is not in the Department of Management's published data, so no debt figure is given and debt is not scored.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Iowa county candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Iowa yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 2 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Cedar Falls's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, as the city reported them in its Annual Financial Report to the Iowa Department of Management. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Black Hawk County.

Spending is reported by program for every fund, enterprise funds included. Capital projects have no program, so they are spread over the city's other spending in proportion; enterprise capital outlay counts as utilities.
Internal service funds (self-insurance, central garages and the like; $8,960 of their revenue and spending) are left out, since the departments they serve report that spending.
Borrowing, transfers between funds, internal TIF loans and sales of capital assets are left out.
General government and community and economic development (including TIF rebates to developers) count as overhead.
Debt outstanding is not in the Department of Management's published data, so no debt figure is given and debt is not scored.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Iowa city candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
Cameras: no license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of La Porte City's borders in OpenStreetMap as of 2026-10-18.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Iowa yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 2 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Waterloo's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
